strategies.name: Carry Trade with Volatility Timing
strategies.description: Long high-yield currencies, short low-yield currencies. The forward rate bias (violation of uncovered interest parity) is the most robust anomaly in FX. Enhanced with volatility timing: reduce position when FX realized vol spikes (carry unwind protection). Valuation adjustment (PPP-based) further boosts Sharpe from 0.47 to 0.62.
strategies.source: Koijen, Moskowitz & Pedersen (2018) 'Carry' JFE; Burnside, Eichenbaum & Rebelo (2011) 'Carry Trades and Risk' NBER; Macrosynergy (2024) 'Advanced FX Carry with Valuation Adjustment'; Daniel, Hodrick & Lu (2017) 'The Carry Trade' Critical Finance Review; AQR Alternative Thinking 2025 Q1
strategies.implementation_notes: Our version uses 20d momentum filter + 50d SMA + RSI<75. MISSING: (1) volatility timing — reduce/exit when 20d realized vol > 1.5x 60d avg, (2) valuation adjustment — weight by PPP deviation, (3) portfolio construction — should be long top-3 yield, short bottom-3 yield across 8+ pairs. Current implementation only goes long high-yield pairs, missing the short leg which provides hedge during carry unwinds.

parameters.lookback_momentum: 1-12 months (12m optimal per Moskowitz et al.)

strategies.name: FX Time-Series Momentum (TSMOM)
strategies.description: Go long currencies with positive past returns, short those with negative past returns. The 12-month lookback with 1-month holding period is the canonical specification. Works across all major and EM currencies. Returns are distinct from carry — low correlation means combining carry + TSMOM significantly improves portfolio Sharpe.
strategies.source: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012) 'Time Series Momentum' JFE; Menkhoff, Sarno, Schmeling & Schrimpf (2012) 'Currency Momentum Strategies' JFE; AQR TSMOM Factor Dataset (updated monthly through 2025); BIS Working Paper 366 'Currency Momentum Strategies'
strategies.implementation_notes: Our session_momentum_continuation only looks at 1-day moves (>0.4%) with MACD confirmation. This is NOT true TSMOM. True TSMOM uses 12-month lookback, signs the position based on past 12m return, and holds for 1 month. NEED: (1) proper 12m lookback signal, (2) cross-sectional component — long top quintile, short bottom quintile, (3) monthly rebalance, (4) volatility-scaled positions (target 10% annualized vol per position). Transaction costs matter: bid-ask spreads lower profitability significantly for EM pairs.

strategies.name: FX Volatility Risk Premium (VRP) Harvesting
strategies.description: Systematically sell FX options (straddles/strangles) and delta-hedge. Implied volatility consistently exceeds realized volatility in FX markets, creating a persistent risk premium. Machine learning models (gradient boosting on macro features) can time when the VRP is widest, improving Sharpe from ~1.0 to 2.0+.
strategies.source: Sorokin (2016) 'Systematic Delta-Hedging in FX Options' SSRN; ScienceDirect (2022) 'Trading the FX VRP with ML and Alternative Data'; Quantpedia 'Volatility Risk Premium Effect'; Hedge Fund Journal 'Harvesting the VRP Globally'
strategies.implementation_notes: NOT implemented. This is the highest-Sharpe strategy in FX but requires options market access. Implementation path: (1) Sell 1-week ATM straddles on EUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPY, (2) Delta-hedge daily, (3) Use implied-realized vol spread as sizing signal — larger position when spread is wide, (4) Exit or reduce when VIX spikes >25. PROXY without options: trade Bollinger Band mean reversion when BB width > 2x 60d average (captures the same vol compression → expansion cycle). Our forex_bollinger_squeeze partially captures this.

strategies.name: PPP-Based Value Mean Reversion
strategies.description: Trade currencies back toward purchasing power parity fair value. Currencies that are cheap (undervalued vs PPP) tend to appreciate over 1-5 year horizons. Half-life of PPP reversion is ~4 years, but combining with momentum timing (enter only when momentum confirms) shortens effective holding to 3-12 months. The OECD Big Mac Index and relative CPI are common fair-value measures.
strategies.source: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen (2013) 'Value and Momentum Everywhere' JFE; Macrosynergy (2024) 'Advanced FX Carry with Valuation Adjustment'; Frankel & Rose (1996) NBER; Arghyrou (2026) 'Exchange Rate Risk and PPP Deviations' IJFE; Cogent Economics (2025) 'PPP Revisited: Panel Study with Structural Breaks'
strategies.implementation_notes: Our forex_mean_reversion_200d uses z-score from 200d SMA — this is a TECHNICAL mean reversion, not fundamental PPP-based. TRUE PPP value: (1) compute real exchange rate = nominal rate * (foreign CPI / domestic CPI), (2) compare to 5-year or 10-year average, (3) z-score > 1.5 = overvalued (sell), z-score < -1.5 = undervalued (buy). OECD publishes PPP data quarterly. Key improvement: combine PPP value signal with our carry signal — Macrosynergy 2024 shows this lifts Sharpe from 0.47 to 0.62.

parameters.momentum_confirmation: 3-month return must align with value direction

strategies.name: COT Positioning Contrarian Strategy
strategies.description: Use CFTC Commitment of Traders data to identify extreme speculative positioning. When non-commercial (speculative) net position reaches historical extremes (>90th or <10th percentile over 3 years), fade the crowd. Large speculators tend to be right in trends but wrong at turning points. The signal is weekly (Tuesday data, Friday release).
strategies.source: CFTC COT Reports (weekly); EarnForex COT Strategy Backtest (2016-2024); Tradeciety COT Analysis; BIS research on speculative positioning and FX returns
strategies.implementation_notes: NOT implemented. Data source: CFTC weekly COT reports (free, published every Friday). Implementation: (1) Download COT data for CME FX futures (EUR, GBP, JPY, AUD, CAD, CHF, NZD, MXN), (2) Compute net speculative position = non-commercial long - non-commercial short, (3) Z-score over 156 weeks (3 years), (4) Signal: z > 1.5 = crowded long → SELL, z < -1.5 = crowded short → BUY, (5) Confirm with 20d price momentum turning. Hold until z reverts to [-0.5, 0.5]. Profitable on all major pairs except AUD/USD per backtest data.

strategies.name: Dollar Smile Regime Strategy
strategies.description: Trade USD based on the 'Dollar Smile' framework (Stephen Jen / Morgan Stanley, 2001): USD strengthens in both risk-off (safe haven) AND US-growth-outperformance (right side of smile). USD weakens when global growth is synchronized. Classify regime using VIX + US vs. global PMI differential, then position accordingly.
strategies.source: Stephen Jen / Morgan Stanley (2001, reaffirmed 2024-2025); Morgan Stanley 'Why the Dollar Still Smiles' (June 2025); Volity 'Dollar Smile Theory in Forex' (2024); FusionMarkets 'Interest Rate Divergence 2025'
strategies.our_strategy: dxy_correlation_regime + jpy_risk_off (capture parts of the smile)
strategies.implementation_notes: Our dxy_correlation_regime trades DXY trends (middle of smile) and jpy_risk_off captures the left side. MISSING: (1) Unified regime classifier — use VIX level + ISM PMI vs. global PMI to determine which 'phase' we're in, (2) Right side of smile — when US PMI > global PMI by >3 points AND VIX < 20, go long USD vs. EUR/GBP/AUD, (3) Left side — when VIX > 25, long USD vs. risk currencies (AUD, NZD, CAD, EM), (4) Middle — when VIX 15-20 and PMIs synchronized, short USD vs. high-yielders. Morgan Stanley confirmed framework still valid despite 11% USD decline in 2025.

parameters.position_sizing: 1x for trend, 0.5x for counter-trend regime shifts
parameters.rebalance: weekly or on VIX regime change

strategies.name: Macro Event Straddle (FOMC / NFP / CPI)
strategies.description: Trade the volatility expansion around scheduled macro events. Two approaches: (1) Pre-event: buy volatility (straddle) before FOMC/NFP/CPI when implied vol is low vs. historical event-day realized vol. (2) Post-event: trade the breakout direction after the initial 15-min spike settles, using the event-day range as support/resistance. The Fed Funds Futures implied probability vs. actual decision creates the largest moves.
strategies.source: Federal Reserve FEDS Paper 2025-022 'Investor Attention and News Announcements'; FXEmpire 'News-driven FX Trading' (2025); QuantifiedStrategies.com 'NFP Trading Strategy Backtest'; FBS Academy 'Trading Strategy on NFP and CPI Releases' (2024)
strategies.implementation_notes: NOT implemented. Challenging with daily data — requires intraday. PRACTICAL approach with daily bars: (1) Identify FOMC dates (8x/year), NFP (12x/year), CPI (12x/year), (2) On event day, if |daily move| > 1.5x ATR(14), enter continuation trade next day in same direction, (3) TP = 1.5x ATR, SL = 1x ATR, (4) Key: compare actual vs. consensus — surprise magnitude drives the move. WARNING: spreads widen dramatically during events (EUR/USD from 1 pip to 10+ pips). Only trade AFTER the initial spike, not during.

parameters.entry_timing: next day open after event day close

strategies.name: Retail Sentiment Contrarian (SSI/IG Client Sentiment)
strategies.description: Fade retail positioning extremes. When >70% of retail traders are long a pair, go short (and vice versa). Retail traders are statistically net losers (74-89% lose money per ESMA data), making their aggregate positioning a reliable contrarian indicator. Works best in trending markets where retail fights the trend.
strategies.source: DailyFX SSI (Speculative Sentiment Index); IG Client Sentiment Data (free, real-time); FXSSI Retail Sentiment; ESMA (2018) 'Measures on CFDs' — 74-89% retail loss rate; Dukascopy SWFX Sentiment Index
strategies.implementation_notes: NOT implemented. Free data sources: DailyFX SSI (updated twice daily), IG Client Sentiment (real-time), FXSSI (multiple brokers). Implementation: (1) Scrape retail sentiment ratio for each major pair, (2) Signal: >70% retail long → SELL, >70% retail short → BUY, (3) Confirm with ADX > 20 (trending market required), (4) Stronger signal when sentiment is extreme AND price is making new highs/lows in the opposite direction. NOT a standalone strategy — best as confirmation filter for carry/momentum signals.

strategies.name: Interest Rate Differential Momentum (Forward Rate Bias)
strategies.description: Exploit the forward rate bias: high-yield currencies depreciate LESS than the forward rate implies (or appreciate). This is the theoretical foundation of carry trade but implemented differently — focus on CHANGES in rate differentials rather than levels. When a central bank surprises hawkish (rate > expected), go long that currency for 1-3 months. BOJ hiking in Jan 2025 (first in 17 years) was a textbook signal for JPY strength.
strategies.source: FusionMarkets 'Interest Rate Divergence 2025'; Macrosynergy 'Explaining FX Forward Bias' (2024); Fama (1984) 'Forward and Spot Exchange Rates' JME; AInvest 'Central Bank Policy Divergence 2025'
strategies.implementation_notes: Our carry_trade_momentum uses static yield differentials. MISSING: (1) Rate CHANGE signal — when a central bank raises/cuts unexpectedly vs. OIS-implied rate, enter immediately, (2) Track Fed Funds Futures, ECB deposit rate, BOJ rate, BOE rate, RBA rate, RBNZ rate, BOC rate, (3) Signal: hawkish surprise = rate > OIS-implied → long that currency for 1-3 months, (4) Key 2025 context: ECB cut from 3.00% to 2.50% (Jan-Mar 2025), BOJ hiked 0.25% (Jan 2025) — these divergences drove EUR/JPY and USD/JPY trends.

strategies.name: Cross-Currency Basis / Triangular Arbitrage Proxy
strategies.description: Exploit temporary mispricings between related currency pairs. True triangular arbitrage (e.g., EUR/USD * USD/JPY vs. EUR/JPY) is arbitraged away in milliseconds by HFT. But cross-currency BASIS (the cost of swapping currencies via FX swaps vs. interest rate differential) shows persistent dislocations, especially around quarter-end and year-end. Trade the basis when it widens beyond 2 standard deviations.
strategies.source: BIS 'Arbitrage in FX Markets' Working Paper; Wikipedia 'Triangular Arbitrage'; AdmiralMarkets 'Forex Arbitrage Strategy 2026'; FinanceMagnates 'Arbitrage, HFT, Quant Strategies in FX'
strategies.expected_wr: 60-70% (basis trades); near-100% theoretical (pure arb, but captured by HFT)
strategies.implementation_notes: NOT directly implementable without institutional FX swap access. PROXY approach: (1) Monitor EUR/USD * USD/JPY vs. EUR/JPY synthetic — if deviation > 20 pips, the pair with wider spread is mispriced, (2) Statistical arbitrage: compute rolling correlation between related pairs (e.g., AUD/USD and NZD/USD, r > 0.85), trade the spread when z-score > 2, (3) Quarter-end/year-end basis widening is predictable — USD funding stress causes EUR/USD basis to blow out. This is more relevant for institutional than retail. Our community_forex_zscore_mean_reversion partially captures the stat-arb concept.
